Esox lucius: Lures or dead bait can be effective. Use an appropriate wire trace, strong tackle and suitable unhooking tools; handle pike carefully.
Perca fluviatilis: Try small lures or worms around cover and changes in depth.
Cyprinus carpio: Boilies, pellets, sweetcorn and worms are commonly used, with tackle suited to the size of the fish.
Rutilus rutilus: Float fish with maggots, bread or small pieces of worm; light tackle can help.
Abramis brama: Try feeder or float fishing with maggots, worms or sweetcorn.
Salmo trutta: Flies, small lures or bait can work where permitted. Check the local season and tackle rules.
Squalius cephalus: Try bread, worms or small lures near cover and flowing water.
Leuciscus cephalus: Try bread, worms or small lures near cover and flowing water.
Tinca tinca: Try worms, corn or pellets near weed and other cover.
Barbus barbus: On suitable rivers, try a feeder or bottom bait such as pellets, meat or worms in flowing water.
Scardinius erythrophthalmus: Float fish with maggots, bread or small baits around vegetation.
Alburnus alburnus: A small float, fine hook and maggot or tiny piece of bread are common tactics.
Carassius carassius: Try small baits, such as maggots or soft pellets, with a sensitive float near vegetation.
Anguilla anguilla: Eels have special protections in many places. Check local rules and handling requirements before fishing.
Sander lucioperca: Lures or dead baits are used where permitted; use suitable predator tackle and a trace.
Salmo salar: Salmon fishing is tightly regulated. Where permitted, fly or lure tackle may be used; check season, licence and catch-and-release rules.
Oncorhynchus mykiss: Flies, small lures or bait can work depending on the fishery’s rules.
Thymallus thymallus: Small flies and nymphs are common choices in suitable flowing water; check local rules and seasons.
Gadus morhua: Boat or shore anglers often use baited rigs or lures, depending on conditions and local rules.
Dicentrarchus labrax: Lures or natural baits can be fished from shore or boat; check current bass retention and fishing rules.
Scomber scombrus: Small shiny lures and feather rigs are commonly used from shore or boat.
Platichthys flesus: Bottom rigs with worm or other natural bait are commonly used in estuaries and coastal waters.
Pleuronectes platessa: Anglers often use bottom rigs with worm or shellfish bait on sandy ground.
Mugil cephalus: Bread-based baits and light float tackle are often used for mullet; approach quietly.
Liza ramada: Bread-based baits and light float tackle are often used for mullet; approach quietly.
Sparus aurata: Shore and boat anglers use natural baits or lures; local conditions and regulations matter.
Scyliorhinus canicula: Shore or boat anglers use small bottom baits; handle carefully and observe local rules.
